# Wedge skirt attachment, D31 (generated by `python -m rnd.parts.covers`)

The TPU 95A comb skirt (covers.wedge_skirt, PIP_WEDGE_GUARD=skirt) is held on the PETG yaw hood by **12 integral push-in pins**: Ø3 stem through the 2.2 mm hood wall, a barbed cone head Ø5.4 → Ø2.4 × 2.5 mm that snaps behind it, into Ø3.2 holes in the hood (the only hood change). No bond (TPU-to-PETG adhesion is poor and a glued skirt is a hood-plus-skirt replacement), nothing rigid on the hood's outer face (it would stand inside the 25.5 mm hood-to-torso gap and the skirt's 0.2 mm stack margin). Fitted and replaced from outside with the arm assembled: peel off pin by pin, press the new one on (each pin through the slot between two fins, or astride the last fin, with a blunt 3 mm tool).

**Result: ✅** every pin has the hood wall and the skirt's sheet round it and its head ≥ 2 mm from every part riding with the hood (smallest 2.7 mm); worst pin load 11.3 N against 20 N retention (SF 1.8, ≥ 1.5 asked; ESTIMATE until the coupon below). Pins 0.7 g per skirt. The skirt's outer shape is unchanged, so its soft-guard rule (rnd/pinch.py item 7: wall, slots, no TPU crushed) and the probe sweep see the same skirt; the Ø3.2 holes are far below the Ø12 probe.

**Why there is no pin in the middle:** over x −95…−64 above z −34, and under the whole top strip west of x −56, the yaw can stands 3.0 mm inside the hood wall: no head fits there with 2 mm to spare. That ≈ 33 × 50 mm field is held on three sides (bottom row, rear and front columns) and the comb stiffens it (each fin is a 10 mm deep TPU plate in the y–z plane); a finger pulling a fin there lifts the sheet a few mm (ESTIMATE), it does not come off.

## Loads (per pin, ESTIMATE)

Basis: the brief's ≈ 2 N per 10 mm of fin bent over (rnd/pinch.py soft-guard row: 2.1 N), TPU 95A.

| Case | Model | N per pin |
|---|---|---|
| finger, sideways | a 20 mm finger lays 4 fins over along its width: 16 N, shared by 2 pins | 8.0 shear |
| finger, fin-root moment | that force × the 8.5 mm fin height across the 12 mm pin row, on one pin | 11.3 tension |
| static part lays fins over | pushes the sheet onto the hood (no peel); drag μ 1.0 on 3 fins × 30 mm, 3 pins | 6.0 shear |
| tug on a fin | 20 N outward, 2 pins | 10.0 tension |

Capacity: pull-out ≥ 20 N, push-in ≤ 40 N per pin (design targets, ESTIMATE: the head's 1.1 mm undercut on Ø3.2 has to fold back to pass). Stem shear (Ø3 TPU, ≈ 15 MPa) ≈ 100 N and PETG bearing are not limiting. **Coupon (proposed):** 6 pins printed as below on a TPU strip, a 2.2 mm PETG plate with Ø3.2 holes printed horizontal; push-in ≤ 40 N, pull-out ≥ 20 N each, 5 refits without a pin tearing.

## Print orientation

- **Skirt (TPU 95A):** on its inboard-face fin tips, hood side up (build +Y). The inboard-face pins print straight up, the two edge pins at 45°; the top strip and its fins stand as vertical walls; the sheet bridges the 4.4 mm slots. Bed contact 944 mm²; down-facing area past 45° 4327 of 34480 mm² (mostly the slot bridges). Fins that do not reach the bed: x -31 (+2.8 mm), x -37 (+0.5 mm); support those only.
- **Hood (PETG):** top down, open foot up (build −Z). Bed contact 7121 mm², down-facing area past 45° 1853 of 60405 mm². The pin holes print horizontal (inboard face) and at 45° (edge): ream to Ø3.2.

Spacing: the pins sit inside the hood, among parts that all ride on the roll output (no relative motion), so they add no swept or pinch row; the clearance column is to the yaw can, can cap, motor, tension ring, yaw block and rear clevis arm.
